entries.german: Karolus IV, Romanorum Imperator civibus Ratisponensibus indulget ut turbatores pacis et homines facinorosos in civitate Ratisponensi et extra civitatem capere valeant in judicio seu dominio quorumlibet dominorum, et judicare de eisdem, ac suis inimicis et adversariis resistere. D. Nuremberg indictione octava, VI. Idus Julii. (c. S.) Idem civibus Ratisponensibus gratiam quod nec pro imperatore vel rege, episcopo sive duce, vel quoquam extraneo, sed tantum pro suis civibus, si actoribus sive pignoratoribus coram judice civitatis Ratisponensis agentibus indicium et justicia fuerit denegato, impignorari possint aut debeant, confirmat. D. ib. et eod. d. (c. S.) Idem civibus Ratisponensibus gratias, ne a sententiis judicum eorum interlocutoriis vel diffinitivis intra muros civitatis Ratispon. ius reddentium nisi ad ipsorum consistorium in iudicio vel extra aliqualiter appelletur, item ne delictum singularis vel singularium personarum in damnum generale universitatis dictorum civium debeat retorqueri, item ut cives ad nullum iudicium extra civitatem trahi valeant, nec non et cetera privilegia confirmat. D. ib. et eod. d. Idem civibus Ratisponensibus facultatem ut Vngeltum perpetuo duraturum de universis mercimoniis, vino, pane, medone, blado, et aliis victualibus cuiuscunque generis imponere valeant, indulget. Testes: Arnestus archiepiscopus Pragensis, Johannes Olomucensis, Johannes, imperialis aulae cancellarius, Luthomuschlen. Episcopi, Meinhardus electus Tridentinus. ac Illustres Johannes Oppauie et Ratibor, et Bolko Falkenbergen. duces, nec non spectabiles Burghardus Magister curiae, ac Johannes Magdeburgen. et Albertus de Anhalt comites, et nobiles Busco de Wilhartig, Magister Camerae, Johannes de Rosenberg, Sdenco de Sternberg, Rudolfus de Warta, Heinricus de Novadomo, Heinricus de Haksemberg, et Heinricus Bauarus de Bopardia. D. ib. et eod. d.
entries.english: Charles IV, Emperor of the Romans, grants to the citizens of Regensburg that they may seize disturbers of the peace and criminals within and outside the city of Regensburg, under the judgment or dominion of any lord whatsoever, and to pass judgment on them, and to resist their enemies and adversaries. Given at Nuremberg in the eighth indiction, on the 6th day before the Ides of July [July 10th]. The same confirms the grace to the citizens of Regensburg, that they may or should be distrained not for the emperor or king, bishop or duke, or any other outsider, but only for their own citizens, if judgment and justice have been denied to plaintiffs or pledgers acting before the judge of the city of Regensburg. Given at the same place and on the same day. The same confirms the graces to the citizens of Regensburg, that there may be no appeal from the interlocutory or definitive sentences of their judges rendering justice within the walls of the city of Regensburg, except to their own council in or out of court, and also that the offense of a single person or of single persons should not be attributed to the general detriment of the community of the said citizens, and also that the citizens may not be drawn to any court outside the city, and he also confirms other privileges. Given at the same place and on the same day. The same grants the citizens of Regensburg the authority that they may impose a tax (Ungeld), to last perpetually, on all merchandise, wine, bread, mead, grain, and other victuals of whatsoever kind. Witnesses: Arnestus, Archbishop of Prague; Johannes of Olomouc; Johannes of Litomyšl, chancellor of the imperial court, Bishops; Meinhard, bishop-elect of Trent; and the Illustrious Johannes of Opava and Ratibor, and Bolko of Falkenberg, dukes; and also the notable Burghard, Master of the court; and Johannes of Magdeburg and Albertus of Anhalt, counts; and the nobles Busco de Wilhartig, Master of the Chamber; Johannes von Rosenberg; Sdenco von Sternberg; Rudolfus von Warta; Heinricus von Novadomo; Heinricus von Haksemberg; and Heinricus Bauarus von Bopardia. Given at the same place and on the same day.
facts: Johannes de Rosenberg witnessed Emperor Charles IV's privilege grants to Regensburg citizens at Nuremberg
